Let the common exterior angle be \(\theta=\frac{2\pi}{n}\), and set
\[
\zeta=e^{i\theta}.
\]
Orient the polygon so that the side vectors are
\[
\overrightarrow{A_kA_{k+1}}=l_k\,\zeta^{k-1}\quad (k=1,\dots,n),
\]
where \(l_k=A_kA_{k+1}\), with \(A_{n+1}=A_1\). Thus \(l_1\le l_2\le\cdots\le l_n\).

Since the polygon closes,
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n l_k\zeta^{k-1}=0.
\]
Let \(a=l_1\) and \(x_k=l_k-a\). Then \(x_1=0\le x_2\le\cdots\le x_n\), and
\[
\sum_{k=1}^n x_k\zeta^{k-1}=0.
\]
Write \(d_j=x_{j+1}-x_j\ge0\) for \(j=1,\dots,n-1\). Then
\[
x_k=\sum_{j=1}^{k-1}d_j.
\]
Substituting gives
\[
0=\sum_{k=1}^n x_k\zeta^{k-1}
=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}d_j(\zeta^j+\cdots+\zeta^{n-1})
=-\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}d_j(1+\zeta+\cdots+\zeta^{j-1}).
\]
But
\[
1+\zeta+\cdots+\zeta^{j-1}
=\frac{\sin(\pi j/n)}{\sin(\pi/n)}\,e^{i\pi(j-1)/n},
\]
which for \(j=1,\dots,n-1\) lies in the closed upper half-plane, with positive imaginary part for \(j>1\). Hence a nonnegative linear combination can vanish only if all \(d_j=0\).

Therefore \(x_2=\cdots=x_n=0\), so
\[
l_1=l_2=\cdots=l_n.
\]
Thus the polygon is regular, and
\[
\frac{A_1A_n}{A_1A_2}=\frac{l_n}{l_1}=1.
\]

\[
\boxed{1}
\]
